method: Evidence pack from the release file; one Sonnet 5.5 agent established the facts with exact quotes; every quote checked against the release files and README by script; the facts that set the level checked again by hand; level from the fixed rule; label and summary written by Claude Opus 5.5.
label: Downloads and runs a standalone Python on Macs without Python 3.12
summary: The first time you process a whole collection on a Mac without Python 3.12, it downloads a standalone Python (about 25 MB) and runs it, as its README says. It takes whatever the latest release is, then installs the paper-curation packages, which is listed as its own finding.

facts.what: A standalone Python 3.12 build (python-build-standalone, macOS only, cpython-3.12 ...-apple-darwin-install_only.tar.gz for the Mac's chip, currently about 25 MB) fetched from the latest astral-sh/python-build-standalone GitHub release, unpacked into the Zotero profile, then executed. Only fetched when no Python 3.12 is found. The plugin then also runs pip install -r requirements.txt (from the user's paper-curation clone) into a venv built from that Python.
facts.publisher: Astral, who build these standalone Pythons
facts.readmeQuote: 관리형 venv 생성·relocatable Python 다운로드는 컬렉션 전체 처리에서만 실행합니다.

triggerQuote.text: papercurio-toast-runfull-env = Preparing py312 env: { $topic } … (first run may install for a few minutes)

facts.notes: RE-REVIEW of 0.11.0 (sha a0ee0934...) against 0.11.2. RESULT: the download is unchanged. I diffed the old release's papercurio.js against the new one: the embedded BRIDGE_PY block (new lines 7189-7360, old 7256-7427), which holds _plat_tag, _find_py312_candidates, _download_standalone, _ensure_py312 and _pip_install, is byte-identical; so are the JS side ensurePy312 (new 6976-7000, old 7043-7067), runFullViaBridge and the onRunFullCommand trigger region (new ~39640-39700, old ~39735-39795); papercurio-addon.ftl is identical; the file list of the two xpis is identical. Address: same (api.github.com/repos/astral-sh/python-build-standalone/releases/latest, asset picked by name: 'cpython-3.12' and the Mac chip tag aarch64-apple-darwin / x86_64-apple-darwin, ending 'install_only.tar.gz'; new line 7303-7309, old 7370-7376). Check: same, none (no hash or signature; urlretrieve then tarfile.extractall; new lines 7317-7319, old 7384-7386). Trigger: same, right-click a collection > process the whole collection; ensurePy312 runs 'ensure_env' in the bridge before any run, a toast says 'Preparing py312 env ... first run may install for a few minutes', no dialog naming the download (only an alias prompt for new collections). The download only happens when no Python 3.12 is found among Homebrew/miniconda/miniforge paths, PC_PYTHON_PATH pref, PAPER_CURATION_PY312, python3.12 on PATH, or the managed folder. Platforms: same, macOS only ('auto-download supports macOS only; install Python 3.12 manually' raised when platform.system() != 'Darwin'). What differs in 0.11.2 is elsewhere: the whole-file diff is about 315 changed lines, the only download-related line differences being that the old file has an extra ensureBridgeScript() call site and the new file has changed line numbers (about 67 lines earlier) and a Server-Sent-Events 'data:' parsing tweak (new ~7271-7272, unrelated); the README differs only in the connections table rows and bullets (paper-curation connection handling wording), and the README paragraph telling about the download (line 100) is identical. The scanner hit is the BRIDGE_PY template string start (new line 7189); the download function is _download_standalone at new line 7293. Verified existence with gh api: latest python-build-standalone release (tag 20261013) has cpython-3.12.15 install_only assets of 25,180,390 bytes (aarch64) and 24,892,063 bytes (x86_64). Nothing was downloaded or run. All previous facts from the 0.11.0 review still hold.
